```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 7)
```

The SIR model splits a population of size $N$ into three compartments:
**S**usceptible, **I**nfectious, and **R**ecovered (or removed).

$$
\frac{dS}{dt} = -\beta \frac{S I}{N}, \qquad
\frac{dI}{dt} = \beta \frac{S I}{N} - \gamma I, \qquad
\frac{dR}{dt} = \gamma I
$$

Susceptibles become infectious at rate $\beta S I / N$; infectious people
recover at rate $\gamma$. The three equations add up to zero, so the total
population $N$ is constant.

# Solve it numerically with `deSolve`

```{r}
library(deSolve)

sir <- function(time, state, parms) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parms)), {
    dS <- -beta * S * I / N
    dI <-  beta * S * I / N - gamma * I
    dR <-  gamma * I
    list(c(dS, dI, dR))
  })
}

N     <- 1000
init  <- c(S = N - 1, I = 1, R = 0)
parms <- c(beta = 0.5, gamma = 0.2, N = N)
times <- seq(0, 120, by = 1)

out <- as.data.frame(ode(y = init, times = times, func = sir, parms = parms))
head(out)
```

# Plot the epidemic

```{r}
matplot(out$time, out[, c("S", "I", "R")], type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2,
        col = c("blue", "red", "darkgreen"),
        xlab = "Day", ylab = "People", main = "SIR epidemic")
legend("right", c("S", "I", "R"), col = c("blue", "red", "darkgreen"), lty = 1, lwd = 2)
```

# Read off the key numbers

```{r}
peak_I   <- max(out$I)
peak_day <- out$time[which.max(out$I)]
c(peak_infectious = round(peak_I), peak_day = peak_day,
  total_ever_infected = round(max(out$R)))
```

The epidemic rises, peaks when $S/N = 1/R_0$, and then burns out, leaving
some people who were never infected.
